question: Show every product along with its category name.
golden_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name AS product_name, c.name AS category_name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id ORDER BY p.id

question: List all orders with the customer's name.
golden_sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, o.status, o.total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY o.id

question: Show each order item with the product name and order id.
golden_sql: SELECT oi.id, oi.order_id, p.name AS product_name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id ORDER BY oi.id
notes: Roughly 2.5 line items per order on average.

question: Show order id, customer name, product name, and quantity for every order item.
golden_sql: SELECT oi.order_id, c.first_name, p.name AS product_name, oi.quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id ORDER BY oi.order_id

question: Which orders have completed payments, and what method was used?
golden_sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.status, pay.method, pay.amount FROM orders o JOIN payments pay ON pay.order_id = o.id WHERE pay.status = 'completed' ORDER BY o.id
notes: JOIN with WHERE on joined table.

question: Show products and their category names, including products that have no category.
golden_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, c.name AS category_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id ORDER BY p.id
notes: LEFT JOIN preserves orphan rows. With seed data every product has a category, so this is essentially an INNER JOIN, but tests the LLM's choice.

question: How many items are on each order?
golden_sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, COUNT(oi.id) AS item_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.id ORDER BY o.id
notes: Tests JOIN + GROUP BY + COUNT in one query.

question: List customers and any orders they've placed, including customers who have not ordered.
golden_sql: SELECT c.id AS customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, o.id AS order_id, o.status FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY c.id, o.id
notes: LEFT JOIN from the 'one' side. The seeded distribution means most customers have placed exactly one order, so row count ≈ 200-220.
